review.notes: Claims were checked against the linked primary or regulatory source. Evidence and causality are stated conservatively; independent human review is encouraged.

objective: Allocate large performance budgets using marginal traffic, conversion, repeat behavior and direct-booking economics.
businessContext: The travel marketplace depends heavily on search, metasearch and affiliates while cancellation rates, CPCs and direct traffic materially change reported ROI.
strategy: Evaluate channels using incremental traffic, customer experience and anticipated repeat rate rather than a single platform-reported return metric.
outcomes: Booking reported $3.8 billion of marketing expense in 2021 and performance ROI roughly in line with 2019, while direct room-night mix increased versus both 2020 and 2019.
whatWorked: Allocation explicitly incorporated cancellation, conversion, repeat behavior and direct demand.
The company separated performance and brand roles in its reporting.
whatFailed: Public reporting cannot reveal campaign-level incrementality or the exact allocation algorithm.
transferConditions: The advertiser can join spend to completed transactions, cancellations, repeat behavior and direct demand.
nonTransferConditions: Do not benchmark absolute spend or channel mix across businesses with different margins and repeat rates.

sources.title: Booking Holdings 2021 Form 10-K
sources.methodology: Company filing describes channel evaluation factors, marketing expense, ROI context and direct-booking mix.

economicContext: Travel-demand recovery after acute COVID-19 disruption
